title: Shopify’s AI Engine Is Firing on All Cylinders — and the Margins Prove It
subtitle: Revenue up 34%, free cash flow margin at 18%, and the agentic commerce layer is proving additive, not cannibalistic.
summary: Shopify blew past Q2 expectations with 34% revenue growth and an 18% FCF margin — proof that its AI investments are delivering top-line growth and margin expansion at the same time.
bodyHtml:
Shopify just did the thing the skeptics swore it couldn’t: grow like a startup while printing margins like a mature software company. The Q2 2026 numbers aren’t just a beat — they’re a statement. Revenue came in at $3.58 billion, up 34% year over year and roughly $130 million ahead of consensus, while gross merchandise volume climbed 32% to $115.6 billion. That’s the fifth consecutive quarter of 30%-plus GMV growth, and at this point calling it a streak undersells what’s happening. This is a platform firing on every cylinder at once, and for a company this size, that kind of growth is rare air.

The story everyone should be focused on is the AI one. Shopify has spent the last couple of years quietly wiring AI into every layer of the platform — search, cataloging, ads, checkout — and the payoff is no longer theoretical. AI-driven traffic tripled year over year. AI-driven orders tripled. New-buyer orders coming through AI channels convert at twice the rate of orders from other channels, and Catalog AI searches convert at double the rate of old scraped-data searches. Those aren’t vanity metrics. Those are the numbers that change how merchants think about where their next customer comes from, and they’re compounding quarter after quarter.

The important part is what this does to the business model. The fear with agentic commerce was always that AI agents would commoditize the checkout layer — that bots would comparison-shop merchants into oblivion and Shopify would end up running a race to the bottom on fees. Instead, the AI layer is proving additive, not cannibalistic. More discovery, more orders, more new buyers — and Shopify captures economics at every step: the payments, the shipping, the ads, the capital. The more the machines shop, the more Shopify gets paid. That’s the kind of structural tailwind that doesn’t show up in a single quarter’s spreadsheet, but it’s exactly what you want underneath a 30%-plus growth number.

And now the leverage. Operating income jumped 68% to $488 million. Free cash flow hit $654 million, good for an 18% margin versus 16% a year ago. Operating expenses came in at 34% of revenue — roughly four points better than last year. That’s the tell. Revenue growing 34% while expenses as a share of revenue fall four points is not a one-quarter wonder; it’s the compounding curve of a business where the fixed-cost AI investments made in prior years are now doing the heavy lifting essentially for free. The margin expansion is real, it’s structural, and it’s accelerating.

The segments back up the headline. Merchant solutions revenue rose 37% to $2.78 billion, payments penetration hit 68% of GMV — up three points — and Shop Pay GMV grew 53%. B2B GMV jumped 76%, offline was up 32%, and international grew 37%. The B2B number is particularly interesting: it says Shopify is no longer just a small-business story, which changes the ceiling on the entire thesis. Enterprise names like Balmain, Guess, Avon, e.l.f., and Claire’s are landing on the platform, and that matters because the enterprise migration is where the next leg of margin lives. Shopify has claimed roughly half of all incremental US e-commerce dollars since 2025, and nothing in this quarter suggests that share is slipping.

The balance sheet remains the quiet superpower. With roughly $4.8 billion in net cash and a market cap near $187 billion, Shopify isn’t just profitable — it’s a fortress, which means it can keep funding the AI arms race without breaking a sweat. Management guided Q3 to revenue growth in the low-30s with free cash flow margin in the high-teens to low-twenties. Translation: the fear that AI spend would crater profitability is exactly backwards. Shopify is spending aggressively on AI and getting more profitable anyway. That inversion of the usual growth-versus-margin tradeoff is the entire story of this quarter.

This is what operating leverage at scale looks like. The debate for the past two years has been whether Shopify’s AI bets were a growth story or a margin story. The answer, apparently, is both — and the two reinforce each other. As long as the agentic commerce layer keeps compounding and merchants keep consolidating onto the platform, the bull case writes itself.

Disclosure: The Signal holds no position in SHOP. Positions may change. This is not financial advice.
